# Principals, roles, and invariants

## Invariants

| ID | Invariant |
|---|---|
| <a id="i-01"></a>I-01 | Deny by default: an action is allowed only when a rule in this model allows it; missing data, missing context, or evaluation errors deny. |
| <a id="i-02"></a>I-02 | Every request is evaluated inside exactly one workspace tenant context, except explicitly privileged platform operations that run under a separate identity and iterate workspaces explicitly. |
| <a id="i-03"></a>I-03 | Tenant isolation is evaluated first and cannot be granted, shared, elevated, or overridden by any role, grant, or support process. |
| <a id="i-04"></a>I-04 | Access is never inferred from IDs, URLs, relationships, mentions, notifications, search indexes, cached projections, or ownership labels. |
| <a id="i-05"></a>I-05 | Relationships and associations never grant access; containment inherits only scope grants (brand/project) and never share grants. |
| <a id="i-06"></a>I-06 | The all-brands view aggregates authorized records and owns no data. |
| <a id="i-07"></a>I-07 | Inaccessible records, brands, relationships, counts, types, snippets, derived conditions, and related metadata are omitted; not-found and not-authorized are indistinguishable. |
| <a id="i-08"></a>I-08 | Authorization is applied before data contributes to counts, sorting, pagination, calculations, recommendations, AI context, exports, notifications, or webhooks. |
| <a id="i-09"></a>I-09 | Client-side permission checks are presentation only; the server re-evaluates every request and never trusts client-supplied workspace, brand, role, plan, approval, or actor fields. |
| <a id="i-10"></a>I-10 | Ownership (record owner, connection owner) is a responsibility field, not an access grant. |
| <a id="i-11"></a>I-11 | No principal can grant, share, delegate, or configure authority beyond its own grantable authority. |
| <a id="i-12"></a>I-12 | Revocation takes effect on the next authorization check everywhere: sessions, caches, live streams, jobs, agent tool calls, tokens, and external access paths. In-flight external effects are cancelled when safely possible; already-sent content cannot be recalled and is recorded as such. |
| <a id="i-13"></a>I-13 | Plan entitlements can only remove capabilities; they never grant data access. |
| <a id="i-14"></a>I-14 | Execution layers (AI, agents, automations, integrations, tokens, jobs) never have a broader read or write path than the delegating principal and their explicit scope; access can only shrink during execution. |
| <a id="i-15"></a>I-15 | Agents, automations, integrations, and AI can never approve, accept, verify, or decide; only authorized humans can. |
| <a id="i-16"></a>I-16 | Secrets are never readable after storage and never appear in records, permission data, logs, errors, exports, prompts, search, or audit display. |
| <a id="i-17"></a>I-17 | Every material permission change, elevation, support access, and denied high-risk attempt produces an immutable audit or security event. |
| <a id="i-18"></a>I-18 | Field-level restrictions propagate to every derived output: filters, sorts, formulas, conflicts, history, activity, notifications, search, exports, AI. |

## Principal types

| Principal | Class | Description | Data entity |
|---|---|---|---|
| `account` | human | Authenticated person (identity). Holds no tenant rights by itself; selects one membership per request. | `identity.account` |
| `member` | human | Active non-guest workspace membership (owner, administrator, member, limited member, read-only roles). | `tenancy.membership` |
| `guest` | human | Guest membership: access only to records explicitly shared with it. | `tenancy.membership` |
| `team` | grant_holder | Group of memberships; holds grants, never acts. | `tenancy.team` |
| `support_operator` | platform | Platform staff identity from a separate identity provider; no tenant access without a customer-granted, time-boxed support access grant or audited break-glass. | — |
| `api_token_personal` | delegated | Token acting as its creator: creator's current access ∩ token scopes. | `integrations.api_token` |
| `service_principal` | service | Workspace service identity with explicit grants and an accountable owner; used by service API tokens. | `access.service_principal` |
| `oauth_client` | delegated | External assistant or MCP client acting for a consenting user: user's current access ∩ consented scopes ∩ client registration scopes. | `integrations.oauth_client` |
| `integration_connection` | service | Connection identity for sync: mapped brand/project scopes ∩ provider scopes ∩ connection owner's current authority for outbound disclosure. | `integrations.connection` |
| `inbound_webhook` | service | Signature-authenticated endpoint limited to one configured intake action into one configured scope; no read access. | `integrations.inbound_endpoint` |
| `automation` | service | Automation definition's service principal: declared scope and action set ∩ accountable owner's current authority ∩ trigger record scope. | `automation.automation` |
| `ai_action` | delegated | AI action on behalf of a human: initiating human's current access ∩ explicitly selected context; no grants of its own. | `ai.ai_action` |
| `agent_profile` | service | Agent identity with explicit scope grants and tool-class grants. | `agents.agent_profile` |
| `agent_run` | delegated | Run scope = profile grants ∩ assigner access ∩ assignment scope at start, re-evaluated on every tool call (can only shrink). | `agents.agent_run` |
| `tool_invocation` | delegated | One tool call: run scope ∩ tool class grant ∩ approval state of its action class. | `agents.agent_tool_call` |
| `system_job` | platform | Background job with a durable workspace and effective-principal context; system jobs hold only their job kind's allow-listed capabilities. | `execution.job` |
| `anonymous_public` | disabled | Public unauthenticated link visitor. Disabled by default; future capability requiring a separate threat model and OD-27 approval. | — |

## Default roles

| Role | Membership kind | Level cap | Can assign | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | member | — | owner, administrator, member, limited_member, read_only, guest | Implicit manage on all non-sensitive brands and workspace scope; all administrative capabilities; only role for non-delegable actions. Sensitive brands/restricted projects need explicit grants or audited elevation. |
| `administrator` | member | — | administrator, member, limited_member, read_only, guest | Implicit manage on non-sensitive brands; workspace administration except billing ownership, deletion, ownership transfer, retention, legal hold. |
| `member` | member | — | guest | No implicit brand access; brand/project access via scope grants; workspace-scoped records at the workspace default level (view). |
| `limited_member` | member | — | — | Internal user with no implicit workspace or brand access; only explicit brand/project/record grants; reduced administrative abilities. |
| `read_only` | member | view | — | All access capped at view; no comments, edits, or execution beyond policy-enabled read-only AI. |
| `guest` | guest | edit | — | External user; only explicitly shared records at the share level (≤ edit); no scope grants, directory, aggregation, trash, or onward sharing. |

## Access levels

| Level | Includes |
|---|---|
| `view` | read, follow, download |
| `comment` | comment, react, mention, review decision when designated |
| `edit` | create in scope, update, assign, relate, upload, archive, trash, restore, complete |
| `manage` | share, grant scope roles ≤ own, restrict, configure scope, approve brand lines |

## Risk classes

| Class | Meaning | Default controls |
|---|---|---|
| R0 | Informational or trivially reversible internal action | none |
| R1 | Reversible internal change | none (undo available) |
| R2 | Significant internal change or configuration | confirmation; agents need review |
| R3 | External disclosure, financial, access-changing, or integration effect | confirmation + step-up where flagged; agents/automations need human approval or a pre-approved standing grant |
| R4 | Irreversible, production, security, ownership, or legal effect | step-up; independent approver when policy enabled and available; never automatable |

## Approval classes

| Class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `none` | No approval beyond authorization. |
| `confirmation` | Explicit user confirmation (0E confirmation tiers). |
| `designated_human` | A designated human reviewer/approver decides. |
| `independent_if_available` | An approver other than the requester when another approval-capable human exists; otherwise labelled self-approval if policy allows. |
| `two_person` | Independent approver plus step-up authentication. |
| `human_approval` | For agent tool classes: a human approval per action instance. |
| `review_required` | For agent tool classes: changes held for human review before taking effect. |
| `low_impact_policy` | For agent tool classes: allowed without per-action review when workspace low-impact policy enables it (OD-23). |
